summary: Duval County fire tower on Clapboard Creek, described as an 87-foot steel skeleton in a 1934 federal station description. No managing agency, build date or current condition found.

facts.status_note: No source reviewed says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: A federal station description dated 1934 refers to the Clapboard Creek fire tower as an existing structure

evidence.supports: Tower lies on the north shore of the St. Johns River, near the Bayshore Drive bridge over Clapboard Creek
evidence.quote: ON N SHORE OF ST. JOHNS RIVER, 112 METERS N BY W OF END OF THE BAYSHORE-DRIVE BRIDGE ACROSS CLAPBOARD CREEK.
DESCRIBED BY COAST AND GEODETIC SURVEY 1934 (HAP)

evidence.supports: Tower described as an 87-foot steel skeleton structure (about 26.5 m)
Top of the tower is 98 feet above high water
evidence.quote: TOP IS 98 FEET ABOVE HIGH WATER

evidence.supports: Survey station is the peak of a roof of a house on the Clapboard Creek fire tower site
evidence.quote: STATION IS PEAK OF ROOF OF HOUSE ON CLAPBOARD CREEK FIRE TOWER

corrections.current: From: National Geodetic Survey Data Shee
corrections.why: That text is the heading of a NOAA data sheet pasted into the page. The survey office wrote the station description; it does not manage the tower.

notes_for_editor: Sources are a 1934 federal station description (quoted on the Forest Lookouts page) and the NGS datasheet for coordinates. The record height of 26.5 m matches the 87-foot figure in the description. No photos, managing agency or later history found. A search of the Jacksonville Public Library Florida Collection or Florida Memory might turn up history; not attempted beyond one search. The UNF Florida History Online Clapboard Creek plantation page was read and does not mention a tower.
